plugins.name: bruno
plugins.description: Bruno API client skill — .bru file format, JavaScript API reference, authentication patterns, testing with Chai.js, and Git-first collection management.

plugins.name: claudehead
plugins.description: Run Claude Code through the Headroom compression proxy, but only when that proxy passes a real health check — otherwise plain claude. Probes /readyz and /health, requires service headroom-proxy and ready:true, refuses to bind over a foreign port, and starts a detached proxy when none is running.

plugins.name: code-quiz
plugins.description: Before you open a PR, prove you understand the code the agent wrote. Generates a literate explainer of the diff, then quizzes you with five comprehension questions that probe how the change actually works — mechanism, blast radius, design trade-offs, and edge cases. You don't pass until you can explain it. A 'speed regulator' that stops AI from outrunning your understanding (inspired by Geoffrey Litt's explain-diff quiz and usegater.app).

plugins.name: ddd-architecture
plugins.description: Review feature code against DDD and hexagonal architecture principles. Validates domain entities, value objects, use cases, adapters, folder structure, file naming, and test placement.

plugins.name: evolve
plugins.description: Self-evolving skills. Injects a per-skill instructions file (~/.evolutions/<skill>.md, or a folder in your Obsidian vault) on top of every skill invocation and tells Claude to append durable lessons there. You and Claude both edit the file, so skills keep improving without touching plugin source.

plugins.name: feature-planner
plugins.description: Create Phase 0 documentation for a new feature. Generates docs folder structure with plan.md, glossary.md, business-logic.md, architecture.md, errors.md, questions.md, and adr/ folder. Use before any code is written.

plugins.name: git-operations
plugins.description: Git operations enforcer - manages branches, commits, and pull requests with strict naming conventions and quality gates

plugins.name: guide-writer
plugins.description: Write clear, minimal guides — how-tos, tutorials, runbooks — with verified steps, annotated screenshots, and Mermaid diagrams. One reader, one goal, one path: Diátaxis shape, Google-style procedures, Carroll minimalism.

plugins.name: helix-teacher
plugins.description: Teaches Helix editor by analyzing the user's existing configuration, explaining keybindings and LSP setup, and answering questions. Use when the user asks about Helix, their helix config, keybindings, LSP setup, themes, or wants help setting up or learning Helix. Also triggers on "helix keybindings", "explain my helix config", "helix setup", "learn helix", or "hx config".

plugins.name: moon-statusline
plugins.description: Two-line Claude Code status line for moon monorepos: model, moon project and deploy target, worktree, git state, PR on line 1; context bar, cost, lines changed, rate limits, prompt cache on line 2.

plugins.name: neovim-teacher
plugins.description: Teaches Neovim by analyzing the user's existing configuration, explaining installed plugins and keymaps, and answering questions. Use when the user asks about Neovim, Vim, their nvim config, plugins, keymaps, LSP setup, or wants help setting up or learning Neovim. Also triggers on "what plugins do I have", "explain my neovim", "neovim setup", or "learn vim".

plugins.name: node-debug
plugins.description: Debug a running Node.js process via CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol). Set breakpoints, step through code, inspect variables, and evaluate expressions — all headless, no GUI needed.

plugins.name: primehead
plugins.description: Run Prime Agent through the Headroom compression proxy, but only when that proxy passes a real health check — otherwise plain prime-agent. Prime Agent ignores ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, so routing goes through a per-run extension (pi.registerProvider) instead of an env var: nothing durable is written and a dead proxy can never leak into a plain session.

plugins.name: tdd
plugins.description: Test-driven development loop with a human gate. Writes the test cases first as a plain-language list, stops for your confirmation or edits, asks about anything uncertain, then writes the test bodies, runs them to confirm RED, implements the task, and runs again to confirm GREEN.

plugins.name: thinking
plugins.description: Structured thinking tools. Currently ships n-order-consequences: trace second-, third-, and nth-order effects of a decision or change so you don't stop at first-order thinking.

plugins.name: watch-ci
plugins.description: Poll CI checks on a PR until they finish, reporting progress. Use when the user says "watch CI", "monitor CI", "wait for CI", "watch the build", "let me know when CI finishes", or wants to track CI check progress on a PR.
